ideas.title: Icom ID-5200 on D-STAR: Programming, Reflectors and Our First Net Check-ins
ideas.why_now: VHF/UHF is one of our strongest topics (median 2.38x, 80% of uploads above typical), and brand names in titles roughly double first-week views. Our ID-5200 Hamvention hands-on hit 7.11x and the delivery Short hit 4.61x, so viewers want the next chapter. Nets and repeaters are a gap for us (3% of uploads) even though 32% of competitor uploads on that topic double their typical.
ideas.angle: Fits the OPEN YouTube slot on 2026-10-22. This is new compared with the unboxing: a practical setup video covering programming, linking to reflectors, and checking into real nets on air, with the honest frustrations included. Close with a quick verdict on whether it lives up to being a successor to W8KNX's favorite radio.

ideas.title: RTL-SDR Dongle in the Junk Drawer: ADS-B, APRS and Airband in One Evening
ideas.why_now: SDR and scanning is the fastest rising discussion topic by far (lift 6.22x, 57 recent posts). The most discussed community post this week was about getting an unused RTL-SDR dongle on the air, and new free tools for SDRs keep showing up. This is a timely exception: we have little track record on SDR, but the community spike justifies a test.
ideas.angle: Fits the OPEN YouTube slot on 2026-10-29. Pull a dongle out of a drawer and in one evening get aircraft tracking, APRS decoding, and airband listening running, using a live dashboard tool for the APRS and ADS-B part. Different from the ESP32 SDR pitch: this is the cheap hardware most hams already own, aimed at beginners and non-licensed listeners.

ideas.title: FreeDV RADE and WSJT-X JTTY: Two New HF Modes Put to the Test
ideas.why_now: Both new HF modes are moving fast this month. JTTY got updates in WSJT-X v3.3.0-beta1, and its author posted single-page instructions. RADE is getting attention after a national article asked whether it could become the next SSB. Digital modes discussion is up (lift 1.24x) and HF radio talk is up 1.60x.
ideas.angle: Fits the OPEN podcast slot (record 2026-11-03, release 2026-11-05). This combines the hosts' two Hot ideas into one sit-down episode instead of two separate videos. The new angle versus earlier pitches: first-time setup gotchas (being heard is harder than hearing), what changed in the 3.3.0 beta, RADE v2 aiming under 1 kHz, and on-air clips of each mode. End with a plain verdict on which one an everyday ham should try first.

ideas.title: Ham Radio Gift Guide 2026: From Quansheng HTs to the $999 Icom ID-5200
ideas.why_now: Budget radios are underserved by us (4% of uploads vs 9% for competitors) and 34% of competitor budget radio uploads double their typical. Budget and HF radio discussion are both rising (lift 1.50x and 1.60x). A gift guide is also the perfect home for our best topics: new radios and handhelds.
ideas.angle: Fits the OPEN podcast slot (record 2026-12-01, release 2026-12-03), timed for holiday shopping. Walk the price ladder from cheap handhelds and stocking stuffers up through mobiles and HF rigs, using radios we have actually touched this year. Brands and prices go in the title and chapters because both lift our numbers.

ideas.title: Hurricane Watch Net on 14.325 MHz: How to Listen Without Getting in the Way
ideas.why_now: The Hurricane Watch Net is active for Hurricane Isaias on 14.325 MHz by day and 7.268 MHz at night. Emergency comms is barely on our channel (2%) but 27% of competitor uploads on it double their typical. This one is time sensitive, so it should go out as a Short right away.
ideas.angle: Short, no release slot needed, so it can post this week. Tune the net live in the shack, show the frequencies on screen, and give one simple rule: listen and keep the frequency clear unless you have traffic. A frequency in the title follows our numbers lesson.

ideas.title: Listening to the ISS on a Handheld: School Contacts, FM Satellites and New Launches
ideas.why_now: Satellite discussion is up 1.88x, a competitor's 'anyone can listen to satellites' video recently doubled its typical, and new amateur satellites just went up. Hams are also posting about hearing astronaut school contacts on simple handhelds, which is exactly our everyday ham audience.
ideas.angle: Fits the OPEN YouTube slot on 2026-11-12. Receive only, no license needed for the listening part: catch an ARISS school contact and an FM satellite pass on a handheld from Michigan, show the free tracking tools, and point to which of the newly launched satellites are worth watching. This is new compared with the pitched SO-50 contacts video (transmitting) and ISS SSTV video (images): it is about listening first, with a handheld.

ideas.title: CQ WorldWide Weekend on the FTDX101MP: Fresh DX From Michigan
ideas.why_now: Our best Short ever was a CQ WorldWide contest weekend clip at 11.79x. DX is a big topic in community discussion (12% of items) and we have posted 0% on it in the past year. A repeat of that format for this fall's contest weekend is a cheap, proven bet.
ideas.angle: Short, no release slot needed, posted during CQ WorldWide weekend. Quick clips of the band full of DX on the FTDX101MP, a couple of rare ones in the log, and the rig name in the title since brands lift our numbers. It also gives a low-effort bridge from the California QSO Party video in the 2026-10-15 slot.
